lines.caption: This is cc-voice-gateway.

lines.say: Claude Code, hands-free.
Claude's voice mode is great to talk with.
But it can't reach Claude Code on your computer.
The gateway connects the two.
Talk to your Claude Code sessions in the car, with CarPlay or Android Auto.
At your desk, while your hands keep working with mouse and keyboard.
Or on the go, right from your phone.
Ask why the build failed, and hear the answer in a sentence.
Ask for a fix, and a worker changes the code and runs the tests.
It opens a pull request, and tells you how it went.
Behind the voice, three layers of AI work together.
Claude's voice mode listens, and hands off your request.
A controller on your computer keeps the context, steers the workers, and sums up their results.
The workers do the real work, right in your repositories.
Several workers run at the same time.
Across repositories, and side by side in worktrees of their own.
Tasks without code get a work folder: research, a calculation, a draft.
On your computer, or in a Docker container of their own.
Results come back to you as short, spoken news.
If a worker needs you after you hung up, the question reaches you on Telegram.
Checks and reviews on your pull requests are followed up, and review comments get fixed.
And it's safe by design.
Every change lands as a pull request, and a merge needs your yes, twice.
Workers start only on your spoken words.
And emergency stop locks everything, until you unlock it at your computer.
C C voice gateway. Open source on GitHub, as a prototype, provided as is.
